newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-NETS SIGN DRAFT PICK KEITH VAN HORN.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-NETS SIGN DRAFT PICK KEITH VAN HORN.

text.p: The New Jersey Nets signed Utah forward Keith Van Horn, the second overall pick in the NBA draft, to a three-year contract Monday.
Financial terms were not disclosed, but under the rookie salary scale, Van Horn can receive a maximum of $9.161 million over three years.

Van Horn, who was selected by the Philadelphia 76ers and later traded to the Nets in an eight-player deal, becomes the third top-five pick to sign. The San Antonio Spurs signed centre Tim Duncan, the top overall pick, to a three-year contract last Thursday. Forward-centre Tony Battie, the fifth overall pick, signed with the Denver Nuggets last Monday.

"We are very pleased to sign Keith to a multi-year deal," said Nets coach John Calipari. "He is a superb outside shooter and free throw shooter and is an excellent athlete. Keith's signing is another important step forward in our efforts to put a championship-calibre team on the floor."
Calipari coveted Van Horn enough to trade a pair of first-round picks and inherit two other players with multi-year contracts.

New Jersey sent guard Jim Jackson, centre Eric Montross, forward Tim Thomas, the seventh overall pick in the draft, and guard Anthony Parker, the 21st overall selection, to Philadelphia for Van Horn, guard Lucious Harris, forward Don MacLean and centre Michael Cage.
The 6-foot-10 (2.08 metres) Van Horn averaged 22 points and 9.5 rebounds per game for Utah last season as he won his third straight Western Athletic Conference Player of the Year award.

Van Horn finished his four-year college career with a 20.8 scoring average. He shot 52 percent from the field and 40 percent from 3-point range as well as connecting on 85 percent of his free throw attempts in amassing 2,542 points and 1,074 rebounds.
